newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' BOI approves two railway projects.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' BOI approves two railway projects.

text.p: The Philippines' Board of Investments (BOI) has approved projects to construct two railway systems, together worth 239 billion pesos, documents released on Friday showed.
The 200-billion peso Mindanao Railway System in southern Philippines and the 39-billion peso rapid railway project in the northern Philippines were approved during the last board meeting this year.
Both projects are to be undertaken under a build-operate-transfer scheme.

The Mindanao railway, which is to be built jointly by Construcciones y Auxiliar de Ferrocariles, Promet Bhd of Malaysia and Philippines' Euroma Development Corp, will link 15 cities and towns in the southern Mindanao island.
The 2,000-kilometre span will be completed within 12 years.
The northern railway will link the 102 kilometres between Manila and the Clark international airport.

Both Construcciones and Euroma will also be part of the consortium building the north railway, together with Metro Pacific Corp, the Philippine National Railway and Bases Conversion Development Authority, the documents said.
Projects approved by the BOI are eligible for income tax holidays and preferential tariff on imported capital equipment.
